questions.question: Give a brief account on sustainable agriculture.
questions.solution_html:
• Give a brief account on sustainable agriculture.
  • It is a method of farming that aims to produce food while protecting the environment and conserving
  • natural resources. It helps maintain soil fertility and prevents soil erosion. Sustainable agriculture reduces
  • the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides by using natural alternatives. It promotes the use of
  • biofertilizers and biopesticides. This method also conserves water and improves soil health. It helps
  • protect biodiversity and maintains ecological balance. Sustainable agriculture supports long-term food
  • production for future generations. It also helps farmers reduce production costs and maintain healthy
  • crops.

questions.question: How does Trichoderma contribute to soil health and the decomposition of / organic matter?
questions.solution_html:
• Trichoderma acts as a biocontrol agent in the following ways
  •  Competition: Competes with harmful fungi for space and nutrients, preventing their growth
  •  Mycoparasitism: Directly attacks and feeds on pathogenic fungi by coiling around and breaking their cell
  • walls
  •  Antibiosis: Produces antibiotics and toxic substances that inhibit or kill plant pathogens
  •  Enzyme production: Secretes enzymes like chitinase and glucanase that destroy the cell walls of harmful
  • fungi
  •  Induced resistance: Stimulates the plant’s natural defense system, making it more resistant to diseases
  •  Rapid growth: Grows quickly and colonizes the root zone, leaving little chance for pathogens to establish
questions.final_answer:  Rapid growth: Grows quickly and colonizes the root zone, leaving little chance for pathogens to establish

questions.question: Write an account on bioformulations used for the uptake of Phosphorus
questions.solution_html:
• Bioformulations used for the uptake of phosphorus are biological products that contain beneficial
  • microorganisms capable of increasing the availability of phosphorus in soil for plant absorption.
  • Phosphorus is an essential nutrient required for root development, , but much of it in soil exists in
  • insoluble forms that plants cannot directly use.
  • Active component of these bioformulations include phosphate-solubilizing microorganisms (PSMs)
  • such as species of Bacillus, Pseudomonas, and fungi like Aspergillus and Penicillium. These
  • microbes secrete organic acids (such as citric, oxalic, and gluconic acids) that convert insoluble
  • phosphates into soluble forms like orthophosphates, making them available to plants. Some
  • microorganisms also produce enzymes like phosphatases that mineralize organic phosphorus
  • compounds.
  • Mycorrhizal fungi(VAM fungi), also form symbiotic associations with plant roots. Their hyphal
  • network extends into the soil, increasing the surface area for absorption and enhancing
  • phosphorus uptake from distant soil zones.
  • Bioformulations are prepared by mixing these beneficial microbes with carriers such as peat
  • lignite, or compost, and are applied as seed treatment, soil application, or root dipping. Their use
  • improves phosphorus use efficiency, reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers, enhances soil
  • fertility, and supports sustainable agriculture.
questions.final_answer: fertility, and supports sustainable agriculture
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a comparative account on wettable powder and dust type of / bioformulations
questions.solution_html:
• Wettable powder (WP) bioformulations are dry, fine powders containing beneficial microorganisms
  • along with carriers and wetting agents. They are mixed with water before application and applied
  • as sprays, seed treatments, or soil drenches. Dust type bioformulations, on the other hand, are dry
  • formulations where microbial cultures are mixed with inert carriers like talc or ash and applied
  • directly in powder form. They are mainly used for seed dressing or soil application without mixing
  • in water.
  •  Wettable powders require mixing with water; dust formulations are applied directly.
  •  Wettable powders provide uniform application; dust types may be uneven.
  •  Wettable powders adhere better to plant surfaces; dust types have lower adhesion.
  •  Dust formulations are easier and quicker to apply; wettable powders need preparation.
  •  Wettable powders are generally more efficient; dust types are less precise in application.
questions.final_answer:  Wettable powders are generally more efficient; dust types are less precise in application
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Give a brief account on potash-solubilising bio-fertilizers.
questions.solution_html:
• Give a brief account on potash-solubilising bio-fertilizers.
  • Potash-solubilising biofertilizers (KSB) are microbial formulations that help in making potassium
  • (potash) available to plants from insoluble sources in the soil. Potassium is an essential nutrient
  • required for overall plant growth, but a large portion of soil potassium remains in unavailable
  • mineral forms.
  • These biofertilizers contain beneficial microorganisms such as Bacillus sp, and certain species of
  • Pseudomonas. They solubilize potassium-bearing minerals by producing organic acids and other
  • compounds that release potassium into a soluble form that plants can absorb.
  • Potash-solubilising biofertilizers are usually applied as seed treatment, soil application, or mixed
  • with compost. Their use enhances potassium uptake, improves crop yield and quality, and
  • increases resistance to stress conditions such as drought and disease.
questions.final_answer: increases resistance to stress conditions such as drought and disease
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe biodegradable waste and its importance in compost production.
questions.solution_html:
• Biodegradable waste refers to organic materials that can be broken down naturally by
  • microorganisms like bacteria and fungi into simpler substances. Examples include kitchen waste
  • (vegetable peels, fruit scraps), garden waste (leaves, grass), and animal waste.

  •  It serves as the main raw material for making compost.
  •  Microorganisms decompose biodegradable waste into nutrient-rich humus.
  •  It improves soil fertility by adding essential nutrients.
  •  It enhances soil structure and water-holding capacity.
  •  It promotes the growth of beneficial soil microbes.
  •  It reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills.
  •  It is an eco-friendly way of waste management.
  •  It supports sustainable agriculture by reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
  • Essay

questions.question: Discuss ectomycorrhiza as a biofertilizer.
questions.solution_html:
• Ectomycorrhiza is a beneficial relationship between certain fungi and the roots of plants
  • especially trees like pine, oak, and eucalyptus. In this association, the fungus forms a sheath
  • around the roots and helps the plant absorb nutrients from the soil, while the plant
  • provides food (sugars) to the fungus.
  • Ectomycorrhiza plays an important role in improving plant growth naturally without using
  • chemicals. It plays a key role in sustainable agriculture and forest management.
  • Functions and role
  •  The fungal threads spread into the soil and increase the root’s ability to absorb nutrients.
  •  It helps in better uptake of important nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen.
  •  It also improves water absorption, especially in dry conditions.
  •  The fungus protects plant roots from harmful pathogens (disease-causing organisms).
  • Advantages
  •  Improves nutrient uptake, especially phosphorus.
  •  Enhances plant growth and survival.
  •  Increases resistance to diseases and environmental stress.
  •  Improves soil structure and fertility.
  •  Reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
  •  Helps plants grow well even in poor soils.
  •  Eco-friendly and safe for the environment.
questions.final_answer:  Eco-friendly and safe for the environment
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the isolation, mass multiplication, and formulation of Rhizobium as a / biocontrol agent.
questions.solution_html:
• Rhizobium is a beneficial soil bacterium found in the root nodules of legume plants like peas
  • beans, and groundnut. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form for plants. It also
  • acts as a biocontrol agent by improving plant health and suppressing harmful microbes.
  • Isolation of Rhizobium
  • Isolation is the process of obtaining a pure strain. Healthy pink root nodules are collected from
  • legume plants. The nodules are washed and surface sterilized to remove unwanted
  • microorganisms. They are then crushed and spread on a selective medium such as Yeast
  • Extract Mannitol Agar (YEMA). After incubation, bacterial colonies appear and are purified.
  • The best strain is selected based on its ability to form nodules and fix nitrogen.
  • Mass Multiplication
  • Mass multiplication is the large-scale production of Rhizobium. A nutrient medium like Yeast
  • Extract Mannitol (YEM) broth is prepared and sterilized. The selected culture is inoculated
  • into the broth and incubated at 28–30°C. The bacteria multiply rapidly and reach a high
  • population (10 –10 cells/ml). The culture is then ready for further processing.
  • Formulation of Rhizobium Biofertilizer
  • In formulation, the bacterial culture is mixed with a carrier material such as peat or lignite. The
  • carrier is first powdered, sterilized, and moisture is adjusted to about 40–50%. The broth
  • culture is mixed uniformly with the carrier and kept for 2–3 days (curing). The final product is
  • packed in polythene bags and stored at 4–15°C. The shelf life is about 6 months.
  • Role as a Biocontrol Agent
  • Rhizobium competes with harmful microbes in the soil, improves plant growth, enhances soil
  • fertility, and increases plant resistance to diseases. It reduces the use of chemical fertilizers and
  • pesticides.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) The bacteria multiply rapidly and reach a high

  •  Increases resistance to diseases and environmental stress.
  •  Improves soil structure and fertility.
  •  Reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
  •  Helps plants grow well even in poor soils.
  •  Eco-friendly and safe for the environment.
questions.final_answer:  Eco-friendly and safe for the environment

questions.question: Explain the isolation, mass multiplication, and formulation of Rhizobium as a / biocontrol agent.
questions.solution_html:
• Rhizobium is a beneficial soil bacterium found in the root nodules of legume plants like peas
  • beans, and groundnut. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form for plants. It also
  • acts as a biocontrol agent by improving plant health and suppressing harmful microbes.
  • Isolation of Rhizobium
  • Isolation is the process of obtaining a pure strain. Healthy pink root nodules are collected from
  • legume plants. The nodules are washed and surface sterilized to remove unwanted
  • microorganisms. They are then crushed and spread on a selective medium such as Yeast
  • Extract Mannitol Agar (YEMA). After incubation, bacterial colonies appear and are purified.
  • The best strain is selected based on its ability to form nodules and fix nitrogen.
  • Mass Multiplication
  • Mass multiplication is the large-scale production of Rhizobium. A nutrient medium like Yeast
  • Extract Mannitol (YEM) broth is prepared and sterilized. The selected culture is inoculated
  • into the broth and incubated at 28–30°C. The bacteria multiply rapidly and reach a high
  • population (10 –10 cells/ml). The culture is then ready for further processing.
  • Formulation of Rhizobium Biofertilizer
  • In formulation, the bacterial culture is mixed with a carrier material such as peat or lignite. The
  • carrier is first powdered, sterilized, and moisture is adjusted to about 40–50%. The broth
  • culture is mixed uniformly with the carrier and kept for 2–3 days (curing). The final product is
  • packed in polythene bags and stored at 4–15°C. The shelf life is about 6 months.
  • Role as a Biocontrol Agent
  • Rhizobium competes with harmful microbes in the soil, improves plant growth, enhances soil
  • fertility, and increases plant resistance to diseases. It reduces the use of chemical fertilizers and
  • pesticides.
